hook: NASA's Voyager 1 went silent 16 billion miles away, leaving mission controllers waiting in the dark.

sections.voiceover: NASA's Voyager 1 went silent 16 billion miles away, leaving mission controllers waiting in the dark.
sections.visual_cue: Graphic showing Voyager 1 drifting in deep space with distance 16 billion miles displayed.
b_roll: NASA artist rendition of Voyager 1 in deep space

sections.voiceover: On October 18, the Deep Space Network attempted contact with the probe at its extreme distance. Did the Deep Space Network lose contact because Voyager 1 is 16 billion miles from Earth?
sections.visual_cue: Animation of Earth and a radio signal pulse failing to reach the distant Voyager 1 probe.
b_roll: Deep Space Network antenna array footage

sections.voiceover: But Voyager 1 suddenly resumed its radio signal after the October 20 unexpected silence.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a waveform monitor suddenly flatlining then spiking back to life.

sections.voiceover: The communication pause lasted 48 hours before the link with Earth self-corrected on October 20. NASA completed a months-long effort in September to stretch the Voyager 1 power supply capacity.
sections.visual_cue: Timeline graphic showing 48 hour gap labeled as Communication Pause.
b_roll: NASA JPL mission control center interior

sections.voiceover: Voyager 1 remains our furthest messenger in the silent void.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from Voyager 1 into the vast star field.
b_roll: NASA artist rendition of Voyager 1 against distant stars
